Meet MELPA's packaging conventions

package-lint reads every `(any ...)` in an rx form as a call to the
function Emacs 31.1 added under that name, so the sources use the `in`
spelling of the same rx construct. remoto-topic.el now declares its
package-lint main file, without which the linter treats it as a package
of its own and demands dependencies remoto.el already declares.

melpazoid fails a package whose files carry no license boilerplate, and
MELPA asks for an Assisted-by line under the author.

The Embark hook becomes a one-line autoload cookie: package-lint rejects
`with-eval-after-load' as code. The generated autoloads carry the same
form, so installed users are unaffected, but a session that loads
remoto-embark.el by hand must now call `remoto-embark-register' itself.

`make lint' runs package-lint and checkdoc, and CI runs it on every push.

Gate remoto's side effects behind global-remoto-mode (#34)

* Gate every side effect behind global-remoto-mode

Loading remoto registered the file-name handler, advised dired,
find-file-noselect and read-file-name-internal, added three hooks and
started an idle timer. The Elisp coding conventions say loading a
package must not change editing behaviour, and the MELPA review
(melpa/melpa#10219) asked for a global minor mode gating these.

global-remoto-mode owns all of it and remoto-unload-function turns it
off. remoto-browse and the Embark actions that visit a remoto path turn
the mode on when it is off, so users who enter through them see no
change; a bare C-x C-f /gh: needs (global-remoto-mode 1), hence 2.0.0.

Also from the review: the declare-function blocks in remoto-embark.el
and remoto-topic.el were dead after (require 'remoto) and two arglists
had drifted; the Magit call uses an fboundp guard; the auth-source
failure is reported once and marks auth as failed instead of being
retried silently on every call; the Embark catch is narrowed to the
user-error the API layer signals.

* Fix the end-to-end findings

Every HTTP error read "Remoto: API error: HTTP Error: 404, ..." with the
full payload: remoto--ghub-get matched ghub-404, ghub-403 and ghub-401,
error symbols ghub stopped defining in its 2.0.0. The handler now
dispatches on the status code ghub actually signals.

The first API call after a failed auth-source lookup handed ghub an empty
auth, so ghub's own lookup hit the same broken backend and that one call
errored while the next went unauthenticated. The call that discovers the
failure now goes unauthenticated itself.

dired on /github:o/r, /github:o/r/ or a /gh: path opened an empty listing
named after the last path component, and find-file called from Lisp with a
/gh: path skipped the rewrite (empty listing, "cannot parse path" for
/gh:o/r#N plus a stray buffer). Both advices and remoto--maybe-rewrite
normalize the shorthand first and the Dired advice rewrites short forms.

Visiting a path absent from the repository signaled the API's 404 from
inside find-file-noselect, which then left an empty file-less buffer
behind. The handler signals file-missing like TRAMP, recording the visited
name first so the new-file path can go on.

Also: https://github.com/o/r.git parses to repository r, URL path segments
are percent-encoded, and issue candidates carry a display-sort-function so
completion UIs keep the PRs-first order.

* Fix the remaining end-to-end findings

- Keep fetched file bytes as bytes and decode them in the buffer the
  way Emacs reads a file from disk, so image-mode renders remoto
  images and file-local-copy is byte-exact.
- Run fetches that input can interrupt as callback requests and keep
  them for the next call, so an interrupted completion neither leaves
  url buffers behind nor repeats the request.
- Open pull request and issue web URLs as topics in find-file and
  remoto-browse.
- Classify the root Dired of a repository at a ref as the repository
  for Embark, not as a branch.

* Serve the first remoto path without an init line, and show every fetch

A /github: or /gh: path typed at C-x C-f in a fresh session opened a
bogus local buffer: since the switch to global-remoto-mode nothing in
that keystroke called into remoto, so the path fell through to TRAMP's
autoload handler, while M-x remoto-browse turned the mode on itself.
The package autoloads now register remoto-autoload-file-name-handler
for the two prefixes, the way TRAMP's loaddefs register its autoload
handler: the first such path loads remoto, turns the mode on with the
same message remoto-browse gives, hands the operation to the real
handler and leaves file-name-handler-alist. Loading remoto still
changes nothing, and the mode still owns every hook and advice.

The fetch indicator showed only for the background searches, and only
when the minibuffer text began with /github:, so the /gh: shorthand, a
path typed after the shadowed default directory, and every blocking
fetch (branches, tags, issues, the default branch, a cold owner
listing) showed nothing. Every synchronous API call now draws the same
label: the minibuffer overlay while a remoto prompt is up, the echo
area once the chosen path opens, which is what remoto-browse already
did for its own fetch.

A child-Emacs spec loads only the generated autoloads and drives the
first /gh: path from there, so a session that starts at C-x C-f is
covered.

* Fix the last end-to-end findings

The first find-file or dired of a session behaved differently from every
later one. The autoload handler turns the mode on from inside the call
that is already running, so global-remoto-mode installed its rewriting
advice too late for that one call: a short path opened an empty listing,
and a #NUM path signaled "cannot parse path" and left a buffer named
after the number. The autoload handler now canonicalizes the name it is
given for expand-file-name, the operation find-file-noselect asks first
and whose result it visits, and insert-directory resolves a short path
instead of insisting on the canonical one. A #NUM path cannot become a
topic buffer from inside that call, so it says what the path is and
kills the empty buffer find-file-noselect made for it.

recentf dropped every remoto path, and since the autoload handler landed
it also loaded remoto and fetched a tree at startup to do it.
recentf-keep-default-predicate asks file-remote-p whether the connection
is up; remoto answered yes for a repository it had never fetched, which
sent the check on to access-file, an operation remoto did not handle.
file-remote-p now honors CONNECTED, with never reading as nil the way
eshell needs, and access-file answers like the local primitive. desktop
restores remoto buffers for the same reason.

Typing at the @ level fetched the repository's whole recursive tree once
per branch or tag offered, because completion asks file-exists-p about
every candidate it shows and remoto answered that by materializing the
tree. A repository root at a ref is now answered on its shape, as
/github:OWNER/REPO/ already was.

The [fetching...] indicator vanished once the C-x C-f prompt inside a
remoto directory was cleared, although completion kept fetching from
that directory. The prompt is recognized by its directory as well as by
its text.

The rewriting advice sat on dired, so dired-noselect, dired-other-window
and dired-other-frame still opened an empty listing. It sits on
dired-noselect now, which all of them call.

A GitHub token sat in remoto--pending-requests as part of a hash-table
key while a request was in flight, so it appeared in any dump of that
variable. The key carries a hash of it instead.

* Tell the first #NUM call of a session what to do

The error a #NUM path raised said to open it with find-file, and the
caller that saw it most often had just called find-file. That call
reaches the handler only when it started before global-remoto-mode
installed the advice that turns a #NUM path into a topic buffer, which
is the first remoto call of a session; by the time the error is raised
the advice is in place, so running the same command again opens the
topic.

The two callers cannot be told apart by looking for the advice, since
the autoload handler installs it before it dispatches. They are told
apart by the buffer state find-file-noselect leaves, which the branch
already tested to decide whether to kill the buffer: VISIT set, buffer
empty, no buffer-file-name. Anyone else asked for the contents directly
and still gets pointed at find-file.

* Draw the fetch indicator in front of the input

[fetching...] sat at the end of the minibuffer input, where it dragged
the cursor three columns right and back on every keystroke. Emacs draws
the cursor after any string that follows point, and the cursor text
property that used to hold it in place loses to Vertico: its candidates
overlay sits at the same position and its before-string opens with a
space carrying that same property. Nothing drawn after point can win it
back.

The indicator now sits between the prompt and the path, as an overlay
before-string at minibuffer-prompt-end, and its slot stays for the rest
of the prompt, blank between requests, so the input does not shift left
and right either. It is one character, a circle arrow: a text glyph
rather than an emoji, since a color glyph is taller than the line it
sits in and ignores the shadow face.

Open remoto paths with Evil's ex commands (#39)

* Open remoto paths with Evil's ex commands

Evil rebuilds an ex file argument from file-remote-p and its localname,
and remoto answered the prefix for localname, so :e /gh:o/r/x reached
find-file as /github:/github:.  Answer the path after the prefix for the
argument of the running ex command only, with bare # and % escaped so
Evil's alternate and current file substitution leaves remoto paths
alone.  Every other caller keeps the prefix: callers pass localname to
local programs, and remoto runs none.

Closes agzam/remoto.el#38

* Open remoto paths with Evil releases that lack evil-called-from-ex-p

The Evil releases on NonGNU ELPA and MELPA Stable predate
evil-called-from-ex-p, so the split never happened there and :e still
reached find-file with the prefix twice.  Fall back to evil-ex-point,
which every Evil binds around an ex command only.  The README now says
that a relative name keeps Evil's # and %.

List accounts and repositories in Dired at /github: and /github:OWNER/
body.body:
## Summary
Dired on `/github:` and `/github:OWNER/` used to open an empty buffer. It now lists the account of the token and its organizations at `/github:`, and an owner's repositories at `/github:OWNER/`. Closes agzam/remoto.el#46.

- A repository line shows its size, its last push as the date, `drwx------` for a private repository and `dr-xr-xr-x` for an archived one, then its description, with `fork` in front for a fork. An account line shows the account type and description. `-t` sorts by the last push, and `dired-hide-details-mode` hides the descriptions with the other details.
- The first 100 repositories arrive before Dired shows the listing. Later pages load in the background, one at a time, up to `remoto-listing-cap` (1000, the most recently pushed), and the buffer reverts once when they are in. Until then the `.` line says how many are listed; it also says when the cap or a failed page ended the listing. The `total` line cannot carry this, because Dired deletes it under the default `dired-free-space`.
- The token's own account (`user/repos?affiliation=owner`) and its organizations (`orgs/ORG/repos`) list private repositories too. Any other account lists its public ones (`users/OWNER/repos`). Without a token, `/github:` says why and opens no buffer.
- `RET` on a repository opens its root at the default branch. The listing already holds that branch, so only the tree is fetched. `file-exists-p` answers t for a bare `/github:OWNER/REPO` or `/github:OWNER` once a cached listing holds it; an unlisted name keeps the `[Confirm]` at a file prompt.
- `C-x C-f` or `C-x d` on `/github:OWNER/NAME`, where OWNER has no repository NAME, opens a Dired of OWNER's repositories that match NAME: the ones the completion at `/github:OWNER/` found while NAME was typed. So a query submitted as is (the prompt selected in Vertico, or `M-RET`) lists its results; it used to fail with "Remoto: not found: repos/OWNER/NAME". The repository check stays first, a name with a space (an orderless query) is searched without one, and a name that nothing matches says so. The matches open as Dired on a list of names, which takes the place of an open `/github:OWNER/` listing until `C-x d /github:OWNER/` brings it back.

body.title: Tentative: wildcards in a Dired of a repository directory, as TRAMP has
body.body:
Tentative, low practical value. Filed so the gap stays known.

TRAMP takes wildcards in the file part of a remote path: `C-x C-f /ssh:host:/etc/*.conf` visits every match, and `C-x d /ssh:host:/etc/*.conf` lists them. Never in the host part.

remoto already does the first: `C-x C-f /gh:agzam/remoto.el@main:/test/*.el` opens all three files. The second does not work: `C-x d /gh:agzam/remoto.el@main:/test/*.el` opens an empty listing with a `wildcard *.el` line, because `remoto--handle-insert-directory` ignores its WILDCARD argument. origin/main behaves the same.

The levels above a repository (`/gh:agzam/remo*`) are TRAMP's host part and stay out of scope: a name there that names nothing already lists the matches (agzam/remoto.el#47).

body.title: Lisp callers of find-file get a Dired of matches too (org links, bookmarks, desktop)
body.body:
agzam/remoto.el#47 lists the matches of a name that names nothing: `C-x C-f /gh:qlik` opens a Dired of the accounts that match `qlik`, and a file name that its directory lacks opens a Dired of the entries that hold it.

The matches come from the advice on `find-file-noselect` and `dired-noselect`, so every caller gets them, not only the prompts:

- An org link `[[/gh:agzam]]` opens a Dired of the 94 accounts that match `agzam`, not agzam's repositories.
- A link or a bookmark to `/gh:agzam/remoto.el/README`, a file that does not exist, opens a Dired with `README.org` instead of an empty buffer.
- `desktop` and `recentf` reopen a remoto file that was renamed upstream the same way.

Nothing breaks that we know of, but the matches were designed for the prompts only.

To decide:

- Keep the matches for every caller and document it, or limit them to `C-x C-f`, `C-x d` and Evil's `:e`.
- The advice cannot tell a prompt from a Lisp caller. Limiting needs a test such as `this-command`, advice on the commands themselves, or a variable that the prompts bind.
- A link to an account without the slash (`/gh:agzam`) probably means the account, not a search.

body.title: Feat: Dired listings for `/github:` and `/github:OWNER/`
body.body:
Dired on `/github:` or `/github:OWNER/` opens an empty buffer. `file-directory-p` answers t for both, but `remoto--handle-insert-directory` lists only canonical repository paths and prints nothing above them. In a live session, `(dired-noselect "/github:torvalds/")` returns a buffer that holds only the header line `/github:torvalds:`.

Completion already has the data for both levels: your login and your orgs at `/github:`, an owner's repositories at `/github:OWNER/`. Dired could list the same.

Gists need this too. In agzam/remoto.el#40, `/gist:OWNER/` lists an owner's gists and is the main view, so RET there must show something. A listing built once in the core serves both forges. Landing it for GitHub first keeps the gist change smaller.

## Proposal

| Path | Lists |
|---|---|
| `/github:` | your login and your orgs |
| `/github:OWNER/` | OWNER's repositories |

```
drwxr-xr-x  1 github github  9589760 Oct 20 18:48 remoto.el  Browse GitHub repos without cloning
```

- Each name carries the `dired-filename` property, as listing names do since 2.1.1. Dired ends a name where the property ends, so the text after it is not part of the name. A batch probe on Emacs 32 read the name exactly and marked the line.
- The columns carry real data: the date is `pushed_at`, the size is the API's `size` (in KB). A private repository gets `drwx------`, an archived one `dr-xr-xr-x`.
- The text after the name holds the description and a fork mark. At `/github:` it holds the account type and description, as the completion annotations do.
- RET on a repository opens its root at the default branch, as `/github:OWNER/REPO/` does.
- `..` at a repository root goes up to `/github:OWNER/`, and from there to `/github:`. Today `..` at a repository root stays at the root.

## Cost

GET requests on 2026-10-20, one page of 100:

| Owner | Repositories | Pages | Time per page | Size per page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| torvalds | 12 | 1 | 0.5 s | 63 KB |
| agzam | 165 owned, 143 public | 2 | 1.2 to 2.2 s | 513 KB |
| microsoft | 8384 | 84 | 2.0 s | 578 KB |

- Completion uses the search API: the 30 most recently updated repositories, then a search by name. A listing needs the list endpoints: `/users/OWNER/repos` (orgs too), `/user/repos?affiliation=owner` for your private repositories, `/orgs/ORG/repos` for the private repositories of your orgs.
- All of microsoft takes about 3 minutes and 48 MB, so a large owner needs a cap and paging in the background.

## Questions

1. Cap: how many repositories, and how does a partial listing say so?
2. While pages arrive: show the first page and revert when the rest lands, or block until the cap?
3. Order: newest push first, as completion does, or by name, as `ls` does? Honor `-t`?
4. Which repositories: forks and archived ones too? Private ones?
5. Without a token `/github:` has nothing to list. Empty listing, or a message?
6. Once a listing is cached, should completion at `/github:OWNER/` narrow it instead of searching?
7. Vertico: RET at `/github:OWNER/`, in `C-x C-f` and `C-x d` alike, takes the first candidate. remoto replaces the completion category, and Vertico selects the prompt for a directory only under category `file`. The listing then opens with `M-RET` or with `..` from a repository. Is that enough?
8. Embark: its Dired finder must report each line as a repository, or as an account at `/github:`.

## Notes

- The listing shows what completion already shows, private org memberships and private repositories included.
- dired-subtree can expand a repository inline, at one tree request per repository.

body.title: Docs: Info manual readable in Emacs (`C-h R remoto`)
body.body:
Ship a manual with the package that opens inside Emacs: `C-h R remoto RET`, or `C-h i m remoto RET`. It covers every command, user option, face, keymap and Embark action, and its indices let `i` in Info find any of them.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `docs/remoto.org` | The manual. All edits go here. |
| `docs/remoto.texi` | Exported from `docs/remoto.org` by ox-texinfo. Committed, never edited by hand. |
| `docs/remoto.info`, `docs/dir` | Built by `make docs`. Not committed. |

- MELPA's default recipe already picks up `docs/*.texi` and builds `remoto.info` from it, so the recipe stays as is. MELPA does not export org files, which is why the `.texi` is committed.
- Elpaca builds the `.texi` the same way. A recipe with its own `:files` list must include `docs/remoto.texi`.
- The manual is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later, like the code.

## Contents

1. Introduction
2. Installation: installing, turning remoto on (`global-remoto-mode`, activation on first use), authentication
3. Getting started: `remoto-browse`, `C-x C-f`, `C-x d`
4. Paths and URLs: canonical form, `/gh:`, the `/`, `@` and `#` delimiters, accepted URLs
5. Completion: levels, annotations, fetch indicator, related options
6. Files and directories: Dired, caches, `remoto-refresh`
7. Issues and pull requests
8. Web URLs: `remoto-mode`, `remoto-command-map` and how to bind it
9. Embark: targets, keymaps, actions, cloning
10. Other packages: Evil, lsp-mode and Eglot, TRAMP
11. How it works
12. Limitations
13. FAQ
14. Turning remoto off
15. Indices: concepts, commands and functions, variables, keys

GitHub-specific facts (prefixes, token setup, rate limit) get their own subsections. Each new forge (agzam/remoto.el#40, agzam/remoto.el#41, agzam/remoto.el#42, agzam/remoto.el#43, agzam/remoto.el#44) then adds a sibling subsection instead of rewriting chapters.

## Links from the code

- The `remoto` and `remoto-topic` Customize groups link to the manual.
- The docstrings of `global-remoto-mode`, `remoto-browse`, `remoto-mode`, `remoto-command-map`, `remoto-github-auth` and `remoto-inhibited-functions` name their manual node. `*Help*` shows the name as a button.

## README

README.org stays the online overview. It gains a short section on opening the manual.

## Checks

`make docs` exports `docs/remoto.texi`, writes the sha256 of `docs/remoto.org` into it, and builds `docs/remoto.info`.

CI fails when:
- `makeinfo` reports an error or a warning. MELPA demotes `makeinfo` errors to messages, so a broken `.texi` ships a package with no manual and no visible failure.
- The sha256 in `docs/remoto.texi` does not match `docs/remoto.org`. CI does not re-export, because ox-texinfo output changes between Org versions.
- A user option, command, face, mode or keymap has no index entry.
- A docstring names a node the manual does not have.

## Done when

- A package built by package-build from the unchanged MELPA recipe contains `remoto.info` and `dir`.
- In a clean Emacs with that package installed, `C-h R remoto RET` opens the manual, `C-h i` lists it, `i remoto-browse RET` in Info finds the command, `M-x customize-group RET remoto` links to the manual, and the button in `C-h f remoto-browse` opens the right node.

## Out of scope

- An HTML copy on GitHub Pages. That can be a later issue.
- `C-h S` (`info-lookup-symbol`) for remoto symbols.
- A `remoto-manual` command. `C-h R remoto` already opens the manual.
- Images. MELPA's default recipe ships no image files, so the manual is text only.
- A version number in the manual. It would need an edit on every release.

body.title: Feat: Bitbucket support (tentative)
body.body:
Split from agzam/remoto.el#4. Builds on agzam/remoto.el#40, which splits the GitHub-specific code out of the core.

Tentative: remoto might support Bitbucket at some point. This issue keeps the notes until then.

Browse Bitbucket Cloud repositories. Possible prefixes: `/bitbucket:` and `/bb:`.

## Paths

| Path | Shows |
|---|---|
| `/bitbucket:` | your workspaces |
| `/bitbucket:WORKSPACE/` | the workspace's repos |
| `/bitbucket:WORKSPACE/REPO/` | files on the main branch |
| `/bitbucket:WORKSPACE/REPO@` | branches and tags |
| `/bitbucket:WORKSPACE/REPO#` | pull requests |
| `/bitbucket:WORKSPACE/REPO@REF:/PATH` | canonical path of one file |

Bitbucket removed its native issue tracker in August 2026 (the issues API answers 410), so `#N` means a pull request.

## Notes

- REST API 2.0 (`https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0`). `repositories/WORKSPACE/REPO/src/REF/PATH` returns a paginated directory listing or the raw file.
- Cross-workspace listings such as `/2.0/repositories` are gone. Repos are listed per workspace.
- Anonymous reads allow 60 requests per hour, so in practice this needs a token.
- Auth is an Atlassian API token, sent as HTTP basic auth with the account email. App passwords no longer work.
- ghub covers the Bitbucket API (`:forge 'bitbucket`), but its auth code still assumes app passwords. Check it against API tokens first.
- Bitbucket Data Center (self-hosted) has a different API. Out of scope.

body.title: Feat: SourceHut support (`/sourcehut:`, `/hut:`, `/ht:`)
body.body:
Split from agzam/remoto.el#4. Builds on agzam/remoto.el#40, which splits the GitHub-specific code out of the core.

Browse git.sr.ht repositories. `/hut:` and `/ht:` are short for `/sourcehut:`.

## Paths

| Path | Shows |
|---|---|
| `/sourcehut:` | your user |
| `/sourcehut:USER/` | USER's repos |
| `/sourcehut:USER/REPO/` | files on the default branch |
| `/sourcehut:USER/REPO@` | branches and tags |
| `/sourcehut:USER/REPO@REF:/PATH` | canonical path of one file |

`#` is not supported. git.sr.ht has no issues or PRs: trackers live on todo.sr.ht, and patches go through mailing lists on lists.sr.ht.

## Notes

- The git.sr.ht GraphQL API (`https://git.sr.ht/query`) needs a personal access token even for public repos. Without one it answers 401. So SourceHut support needs a token from meta.sr.ht from the start.
- Without a token, raw files load (`https://git.sr.ht/~USER/REPO/blob/REF/PATH`), but tree pages sit behind a bot check (HTTP 418). Directory listings have to come from the API.
- The API returns at most 128 KiB of a text file. Larger files come from the blob's content URL.
- ghub has no SourceHut support, so this needs its own HTTP code (url.el).
- No API call writes a file; changes need `git push`. This only matters once remoto supports writes.

## Open questions

- Keep `~` in paths (`/sourcehut:~USER/REPO`) or drop it (`/sourcehut:USER/REPO`)? Dropping it gives the same `OWNER/REPO` shape as the other forges and avoids Emacs's special handling of `~` in file names. Pasted `~USER` URLs work either way.

body.title: Feat: GitLab support (`/gitlab:`, `/gl:`)
body.body:
Split from agzam/remoto.el#4. Builds on agzam/remoto.el#40, which splits the GitHub-specific code out of the core.

Browse GitLab projects the way remoto browses GitHub repos. `/gl:` is short for `/gitlab:`. The first target is gitlab.com.

## Paths

NAMESPACE is a user or a group. Groups can nest.

| Path | Shows |
|---|---|
| `/gitlab:` | your user and groups, or namespaces matching the input |
| `/gitlab:NAMESPACE/` | its projects, plus subgroups for a group |
| `/gitlab:NAMESPACE/PROJECT/` | files on the default branch |
| `/gitlab:NAMESPACE/PROJECT@` | branches and tags |
| `/gitlab:NAMESPACE/PROJECT#` | issues |
| `/gitlab:NAMESPACE/PROJECT@REF:/PATH` | canonical path of one file |

Groups nest to any depth: `/gitlab:gitlab-org/security-products/analyzers/semgrep@main:/README.md` is a valid path. In a full path, `@` or `:` marks where the project ends, so remoto parses it without a request. Only while completing `GROUP/NAME/` does remoto need the API to tell a subgroup from a project.

## Notes

- REST API v4 (`https://gitlab.com/api/v4`). A project is addressed by its URL-encoded full path (`gitlab-org%2Fcli`). File paths in `repository/files/...` are encoded the same way (`cmd%2Fglab%2Fmain.go`).
- Issues and merge requests have separate number sequences: `gitlab-org/cli` has both an issue 1000 and an MR 1000. So `#N` cannot cover both.
- Anonymous reads work for public projects.
- ghub covers the GitLab API (`:forge 'gitlab`), so no new dependency.

## Open questions

- How to open merge requests. GitLab writes them as `!N`, so `/gitlab:NAMESPACE/PROJECT!N` is the natural choice. `!` needs the same check against Evil's `:e` that `#` got in agzam/remoto.el#38.

## Later

- Self-hosted GitLab. The host stays out of the path, because `/gitlab:HOST:/PATH` has the shape of a TRAMP `/method:host:` name. Each server gets its own prefix through a user option.

body.title: Feat: Codeberg support (`/codeberg:`, `/cb:`)
body.body:
Split from agzam/remoto.el#4. Builds on agzam/remoto.el#40, which splits the GitHub-specific code out of the core.

Browse Codeberg repositories the way remoto browses GitHub ones. `/cb:` is short for `/codeberg:`, as `/gh:` is for `/github:`.

## Paths

Same levels and separators as `/github:`:

| Path | Shows |
|---|---|
| `/codeberg:` | your user and orgs, or users matching the input |
| `/codeberg:OWNER/` | OWNER's repos |
| `/codeberg:OWNER/REPO/` | files on the default branch |
| `/codeberg:OWNER/REPO@` | branches and tags |
| `/codeberg:OWNER/REPO#` | issues and PRs |
| `/codeberg:OWNER/REPO@REF:/PATH` | canonical path of one file |

Issues and PRs share one number sequence, as on GitHub, so `#N` works the same way.

## Notes

- Codeberg runs Forgejo. Its REST API (`https://codeberg.org/api/v1`) has the same shape as GitHub's for repos, contents, trees, branches, tags, issues and PRs, so most of the GitHub code carries over.
- Differences found so far:
  - Recursive trees are paginated. `truncated` stays true until the last page.
  - Search has its own endpoints (`/repos/search`, `/users/search`).
  - Default branch names vary: `forgejo/forgejo` uses `forgejo`.
- Anonymous reads work, up to 2000 requests per 10 minutes.
- ghub covers this API (`:forge 'forgejo`, added in ghub 5.0 with codeberg.org as the default host). No new dependency, though remoto's minimum ghub version (4.0 today) may go up.

## Later

- Other Forgejo and Gitea servers. The host stays out of the path; each server gets its own prefix through a user option.

body.title: Feat: GitHub Gists support (`/gist:`)
body.body:
Split from agzam/remoto.el#4.

Browse and open GitHub Gists the way remoto opens repos: list a user's gists, open their files, read old revisions.

Gists come first among the new sources. They use the same API host and token as `/github:`, so the work can focus on splitting the GitHub-specific code out of the core, one file per forge. The other forges build on that split.

## Paths

| Path | Shows |
|---|---|
| `/gist:` | your login, or users matching the input |
| `/gist:OWNER/` | OWNER's gists, annotated with their descriptions |
| `/gist:OWNER/ID/` | files of the latest revision |
| `/gist:OWNER/ID@` | revisions, newest first |
| `/gist:OWNER/ID@REV:/FILE` | canonical path of one file |

- `@` picks a revision. Without it, remoto uses the latest one.
- `#` is not supported. Gists have no issues or PRs.
- Paths name the owner, not only the id. That keeps the levels of `/github:`, matches `https://gist.github.com/OWNER/ID`, and avoids `/gist:ID:/FILE`, which has the shape of a TRAMP `/method:host:` name.

## Notes

- One `GET /gists/ID` returns the file list and the content of every file, so opening a gist costs one request. The API returns up to 1 MB of each file and marks larger ones `truncated`. Those come from `raw_url`.
- Gists cannot contain directories, so the part after `:` is a flat list of files.
- File names can change between revisions. A file path is valid only at its revision.
- Gist ids are strings, not always hex. Old gists have numeric ids (`/gists/1`).
- Secret gists can be read by id without a token. Listing your own secret gists needs a token, possibly with the `gist` scope.
- Pasting a `gist.github.com` URL opens the gist. The URL commands (copy URL, permalink, raw URL) produce gist URLs.

## Out of scope

- Editing. Remoto is read-only. A gist edit is one `PATCH` request, so gists are a good first candidate once remoto supports writes.

body.title: Feat: jump to a local clone or clone the repo you're browsing
body.body:
When browsing a repo via remoto, provide a command to jump to a local clone (or create one) for full local tooling -
  ripgrep, LSP, magit, etc.

  - remoto-clone-root defcustom - base directory + pattern for cloning new repos (e.g., ~/GitHub/{owner}/{repo})
  - remoto-find-local-clone - scan project-known-project-roots and match git remote URLs against github.com/{owner}/{repo} to
   find existing clones regardless of directory layout
  - Cache the remote-to-local-path mapping (memory or disk) so repeated lookups are fast
  - remoto-clone interactive command:
    - If local clone found, open dired at the corresponding path (map current remoto file/dir to its local equivalent)
    - If not found, offer to git clone --depth 1, optionally check out the ref being browsed
  - Handle edge cases: repo renamed locally, multiple remotes, forks pointing at same upstream

  Motivation: GitHub's code search API has too many limitations (rate limits, no regex, index lag, max 384KB files, only
  indexed branches) to be a practical search solution. Cloning locally gives access to all existing tools with no
  compromises.

body.title: List accounts and repositories in Dired at /github: and /github:OWNER/
body.body:
## Summary
Dired on `/github:` and `/github:OWNER/` used to open an empty buffer. It now lists the account of the token and its organizations at `/github:`, and an owner's repositories at `/github:OWNER/`. Closes agzam/remoto.el#46.

- A repository line shows its size, its last push as the date, `drwx------` for a private repository and `dr-xr-xr-x` for an archived one, then its description, with `fork` in front for a fork. An account line shows the account type and description. `-t` sorts by the last push, and `dired-hide-details-mode` hides the descriptions with the other details.
- The first 100 repositories arrive before Dired shows the listing. Later pages load in the background, one at a time, up to `remoto-listing-cap` (1000, the most recently pushed), and the buffer reverts once when they are in. Until then the `.` line says how many are listed; it also says when the cap or a failed page ended the listing. The `total` line cannot carry this, because Dired deletes it under the default `dired-free-space`.
- The token's own account (`user/repos?affiliation=owner`) and its organizations (`orgs/ORG/repos`) list private repositories too. Any other account lists its public ones (`users/OWNER/repos`). Without a token, `/github:` says why and opens no buffer.
- `RET` on a repository opens its root at the default branch. The listing already holds that branch, so only the tree is fetched. `file-exists-p` answers t for a bare `/github:OWNER/REPO` or `/github:OWNER` once a cached listing holds it; an unlisted name keeps the `[Confirm]` at a file prompt.
- `C-x C-f` or `C-x d` on `/github:OWNER/NAME`, where OWNER has no repository NAME, opens a Dired of OWNER's repositories that match NAME: the ones the completion at `/github:OWNER/` found while NAME was typed. So a query submitted as is (the prompt selected in Vertico, or `M-RET`) lists its results; it used to fail with "Remoto: not found: repos/OWNER/NAME". The repository check stays first, a name with a space (an orderless query) is searched without one, and a name that nothing matches says so. The matches open as Dired on a list of names, which takes the place of an open `/github:OWNER/` listing until `C-x d /github:OWNER/` brings it back.
- `..` at a repository root goes up to `/github:OWNER/`, and from there to `/github:`; `expand-file-name` resolves a `..` above a root the same way. `^` still stays at the root. The short-form rewrite now resolves dots first: it read `/github:OWNER/..` as a repository named `..`.
- `remoto-refresh` fetches a listing again. It is also the retry after a failed page: the revert that shows the failure must not fetch again, or a failing API would loop.
- Embark offers the repository actions on a repository line, and the owner actions on an account line or on an owner listing itself.
- Version 2.3.0.

Known limits:
- Descriptions take Dired's directory face, because Dired paints a directory line from its name to the end of the line. Giving them a face of their own takes the directory face off the name as well.
- A default branch with a slash, such as `release/2026.5.0`, does not parse in a remoto path, so such a repository does not open from a listing or anywhere else; 5 of the 1000 listed qlik-trial repositories have one. That grammar gap predates this PR.

## Testing
- `make test` 744/0, `make test-embark` 66/0, `make test-integration` 22/0 (one new spec lists emacs-mirror), `make lint` and `make check-compile` clean on Emacs 32.0.50. The listing specs fail 34 of 731 on main's code; the 12 matches specs fail 11 of 12 on the first commit's code, the twelfth guards that an existing name still opens.
- Batch Emacs with the real API, authenticated, 40 checks, all pass: `/github:` and `RET` on an account; agzam's 165 repositories in 1.0 s plus 0.45 s in the background; names under `-al`, `-alF` and `-alt`; hide-details; `RET` on a repository with only the tree request; `..` up two levels; torvalds; dired-subtree on a repository line and `RET` on a file in it; Embark on both kinds of line; an unknown owner and `/github:` without a token, each leaving no buffer; `remoto-refresh`; microsoft capped at 1000 after 1.5 s plus 13 s in the background; `/gh:qlik-trial/stitch` listing its 14 matches with only the 404 request and `RET` on one opening it; `dired-noselect` on a name with no cached search; an exact name opening as before; a name with no match; `/gh:qlik-trial/stitch connection` searched without a repository request.
- Live Emacs with treemacs-icons-dired, hide-details and `-aBhlt --group-directories-first`: agzam's listing costs 2 requests (the icons add none), every name reads exactly, the `-t` order holds, `..` climbs, and `/gh:qlik-trial/stitch` opens its 14 matches, newest push first.
